# TestRangeRoundTrip's accepted difference between the targets' decoder messages, ADR-0023 Decision 5: the width of an integer.
# Go and C++ refuse it as `expected an integer from <lo> to <hi>`, or as the short `expected an integer` where the range is Int's full range
# (gen/go text/data.txt jsonInt; C++ IntExpected), and their verdicts are compared as written. TypeScript refuses it as
# `integer out of range`, `expected an integer`, `expected a non-negative integer` or, past a JavaScript number's exact range,
# `integer outside the TypeScript safe range`.
# One regular expression per line. A message of a TypeScript reader that matches one is compared as the same width text, and so is the
# want when it is compared with a TypeScript reader (the first form is the want's, in Go and C++ bytes). Every other message is compared as written.
^expected an integer from -?[0-9]+ to -?[0-9]+$
^integer out of range$
^expected an integer$
^expected a non-negative integer$
^integer outside the TypeScript safe range$
